title: Reliability initiative cadence and OKR mapping
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and launch a repeatable cadence and scoring model to map reliability initiatives (SLO-driven work) to OKRs and roadmap priorities. Deliverables: a scoring matrix, a quarterly initiative cadence, an OKR mapping rubric, and a dashboard prototype that surfaces initiative health relative to error budget runway.
context: We have multiple ad-hoc reliability projects and inconsistent prioritization relative to product OKRs. Engineering and platform teams have requested clearer signals for when to convert engineering effort into prioritized roadmap work vs. short-term operational mitigation. This initiative aims to standardize intake, prioritization, and cadence for SLO-driven work so PMs and Eng leads can make aligned decisions across hosted, dedicated, and private customers.
goals: Create a one-page scoring rubric that ranks reliability initiatives by customer impact, error-budget consumption rate, mitigations available, and implementation velocity
Define a quarterly cadence for initiative intake, review, and OKR mapping aligned with product cycles
Prototype a dashboard view that shows initiative score, error-budget runway, and recommended action (invest / monitor / defer)
Pilot the rubric on five active SLO issues and iterate based on feedback
success_metrics: >90% of reliability initiatives mapped to an OKR or backlog ticket by next planning cycle
Reduction in firefighting: mean time spent on ad-hoc SLO pulls down 25% vs prior quarter
Adopter satisfaction: average pilot feedback >= 4/5 from PMs and Eng leads
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric documented and reviewed by Reliability, Product, and Eng leadership
Cadence doc published in Confluence and added to the planning checklist
Dashboard prototype (Grafana/Looker) showing at least: initiative score, SLI baseline, current burn rate, and projected error-budget runway
Pilot completed and documented with retrospective and 3 concrete adjustments
work_items: Draft scoring rubric and weighting options
Run workshop with Reliability and PM guild to calibrate weights
Build dashboard prototype and backfill with sample SLI data
Select pilot initiatives and run two-week evaluation windows
Write rollout guide and update planning templates
updates: 2025-01-12 — Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting with Reliability (Samira), Platform (Jon), and Eng leads. Agreed scope and deliverables. Action: Miguel to draft rubric.

2025-01-20 — Miguel Santos: Draft rubric v0 posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/rubric-v0. Key trade-offs captured: weight customer-impact higher for Dedicated customers, reserve binary check for compliance-affecting SLOs.

2025-01-28 — Samira Khan (Reliability): Workshop feedback — suggest adding a velocity multiplier to prefer small, high-impact fixes. Miguel to incorporate and run sample scoring on 8 past initiatives.

2025-02-05 — Miguel Santos: Dashboard prototype in Grafana linked to error-budget telemetry created (internal link). Early data shows two initiatives currently mis-prioritized; scheduling pilot starts 2025-02-10.
2025-02-11 — Asha Patel: PM guild review completed. Action items: (1) adjust weight for regulatory SLOs, (2) add OKR alignment checkbox, (3) document escalation path when error-budget < 14 days.
decisions: Adopt three-tier initiative score bands: Low(0-40), Medium(41-70), High(71-100)
Apply a +15 velocity multiplier for fixes estimated <= 3 points to surface quick wins
OKR mapping will be mandatory for High-scored items prior to funding during planning cycles
blockers: Need a stable SLI ingestion pipeline for historical burn-rate calculation — infra ticket ENG-4891 is in progress
Legal requested a short review for initiatives touching customer telemetry; may delay rollout for Dedicated customers
notes_summary: Pilot kickoff next week. Primary risk is timing of SLI pipeline work; if that slips, we'll run scoring manually for pilot. Leadership supports mandatory OKR mapping for high-scored reliability work. Next update after first pilot retrospective (scheduled 2025-02-24).
